question_record.context: A security incident involving suspicious exploration activities was detected. A process on host `mb-winclient` invoked a series of Windows commands using `powershell.exe`. This host relates to several accounts, including 'pwilson'. Some of the commands and processes identified include `powershell.exe c:\script\contosoadfsblatempcreds.ps1` and `whoami.exe /user`. The suspicious activity indicates that attackers may be attempting to identify valuable assets and coordinate lateral movement across the network.
question_record.question: Related to this alert, there was a Windows executable file that was renamed and launched. Can you identify the account name associated with the system executable that was renamed and launched?
solution: A process `powershell.exe` was used to execute a suspicious sequence of exploration activities on 2024-07-04 22:35:03.197761+00:00.
A system executable file was renamed and launched, potentially by a `SYSTEM` account, on 2024-07-04 22:35:01.543723+00:00.

57.name: Suspicious sequence of exploration activities
57.description: A process called a set of windows commands. These commands can be used by attackers in order to identify assets of value and coordinate lateral movement after compromising a machine.

27.name: System executable renamed and launched
27.description: A Windows executable file that has been renamed was launched. Attackers might be attempting to use the executable to perform malicious activities, such as running malicious code or connecting to an attacker-controlled network address. By changing the path or file name of a system executable, attackers can avoid certain behavior-based detection technologies that rely on default paths and file names.

interpretation.scope: official graph witness, not a proof of causality, actor identity or autonomous planning
